thread:
Maya Chen: Heads-up: competitor launched a micro-composition feature that routes sub-prompts to tiny "tiles". Want to discuss parity vs. differentiated approach.
Alex Rivera: I reviewed their docs. It's effectively a thin router + small specialized models. Infra downside: many short-lived model invocations.
Tess Okafor: UX POV: We can ship a "composition" affordance but keep it intentionally opinionated. Avoid making the API a general orchestrator.
Samir Patel: Customers (three pilot prospects) already ask for routing to different models for parts of prompts. This is becoming a check-box for midmarket.
Rita Gomez: Engineering note: we have routing primitives and prefix caching. The hard bits are stateful tile caches and scheduling granularity. I think a 5-working-day spike will surface tradeoffs.
Maya Chen: Proposal: run a focused spike next week to validate perf, cost, and fallback behavior. If good, aim for an early beta with one pilot customer.
Alex Rivera: Spike plan: build a router that splits requests by simple rules (prefix, intent-tag), invoke per-segment model, and reassemble. Measure p50/p95 and token cost.
Noah Li: Add observability hooks: per-segment latency, aggregate end-to-end latency, and fallback counts. Also track memory churn for tiled caches.
Tess Okafor: API suggestion: declarative route list + sane defaults. Example: 
```
composition:
  - when: header.intent == "extract"
    use: small-extract-v1
  - when: otherwise
    use: longform-v2
```
Samir Patel: I'll reach out to PilotCorp for beta permission. If they agree, we can include a co-marketing blurb. I'll update by Friday COB.
Rita Gomez: Risk list for spike: OOM from cache fragmentation, tail-latency due to cross-tile coordination, scheduling overhead. Mitigations: bounded per-tile cache, backpressure, routing-only canary run.
Maya Chen: Draft acceptance criteria:
- P0: end-user p95 < 250ms for our standard light prompt mix
- P0: <1% errors and no degradation on existing single-model routes
- P1: cost increase <= 25% for typical workload unless justified by accuracy gains
- P1: automated canary rollout with rollback on SLO breach (5% -> 30% -> 100%)
- P2: simple docs + example config for common use-cases
Alex Rivera: Suggest first canary be routing-only (no model swaps) to validate infra and metrics.
Tess Okafor: UX will produce two examples: intent-split and content-split. Keep client surface minimal.
Noah Li: I'll pre-provision dashboards and set alerts for p95 and fallback rate.
ci-bot: CI job queued: comp-router-spike -> staging at 4416000038 by alexr.
Maya Chen: Decisions: run spike next Mon. If spike passes, roadmap = spike -> internal pilot -> external beta -> GA + GTM. Timeline tentatively 6 sprints.
Alex Rivera: I'll open the spike PR today, add perf harness. ETA prototype logs Wed EOD.
Samir Patel: Reaching out to PilotCorp now.
Rita Gomez: I'll add benchmark plan and mitigation notes to the spike doc by Thu.
Tess Okafor: Mockups and snippets in thread shortly.
Maya Chen: Thanks team. Goal: minimal parity with a defensible differentiator — predictable costs, rollout controls, and curated examples.
